record.original_question: In the same layered construction G_n(phi), is it true that for sufficiently small nonzero phi the finite sequence of suspension angles phi_0(phi), phi_1(phi), ..., phi_n(phi) never repeats a value? Equivalently, does this force G_n(phi) to be a geodesic net in which all edges have weight one, while still having 14 unbalanced vertices and, for large n, arbitrarily many balanced vertices?

evidence.quote: Lemma 4.5.5. If for any fixed ϕ ∈ (−ϵ, ϵ), the sequence ϕi(ϕ) never repeats itself, all edges of the resulting geodesic net Gn(ϕ) intersect transversally (if at all). In other words, there are no edges with weight other than one.

Conjecture 4.5.8. For small nonzero ϕ ∈ (−ϵ, ϵ), the sequence ϕi (ϕ) never repeats itself. This implies that Gn (ϕ) is a geodesic net for which all edges have weight one. So this Gn (ϕ) would in fact fulfill all required conditions: (a) There are 14 unbalanced vertices. (b) For n large enough, we can achieve an arbitrarily large number of balanced vertices. (c) All edges have weight one.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following layered construction of a planar geodesic net depending on a small angle parameter $\phi$. Fix $\epsilon>0$ small. For $\phi\in(-\epsilon,\epsilon)$, build a sequence of layers indexed by $i=0,1,\dots,n$, where each layer is obtained from the previous one by a "suspension" operation: at each step, the construction is determined by an angle $\phi_i(\phi)$, computed recursively from $\phi_0(\phi)=\phi$ and the geometric rule that two incoming geodesic segments at the apex of layer $i$ are continued so that the balancing condition (the sum of unit tangent vectors of incident edges vanishes) holds at every newly created interior vertex. The resulting weighted geodesic graph is denoted $G_n(\phi)$; it has exactly $14$ designated unbalanced (boundary) vertices, and for $n$ large it has arbitrarily many balanced interior vertices.

A weighted geodesic net is a finite graph embedded in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with edges that are straight segments and positive integer weights $w_e$ on edges, such that at every balanced vertex $v$, $\sum_{e\ni v} w_e\, \mathbf{u}_{e,v} = 0$, where $\mathbf{u}_{e,v}$ is the unit vector along $e$ at $v$. An edge has weight greater than one precisely when two distinct edges of the underlying construction overlap along a common segment.

Prove or disprove: for every sufficiently small nonzero $\phi\in(-\epsilon,\epsilon)$, the finite sequence of suspension angles
$$\phi_0(\phi),\ \phi_1(\phi),\ \ldots,\ \phi_n(\phi)$$
contains no repeated value. Equivalently, show that for all such $\phi$, $G_n(\phi)$ is a geodesic net in which every edge has weight equal to one, while still possessing $14$ unbalanced vertices and (for $n$ large) arbitrarily many balanced vertices.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2024–2025) on geodesic nets with few boundary vertices continues to address related construction problems (e.g., 4-boundary-vertex constructions with increasing numbers of balanced vertices), but no source found explicitly resolves the non-repetition conjecture for the suspension-angle sequence in the 14-unbalanced-vertex layered construction. Status appears unresolved based on accessible sources.
